title: Conventional drill depth and chip evacuation

source.agreement: Read 2026-11-08. Haas mill manual and Hannibal Drill Basics independently agree that conventional drills should peck beyond 3 diameters. This is the agreed threshold used here; specialised coolant-fed and inserted drills have different guidance. Haas distinguishes G73 small lifts from G83 complete exit and restricts high-speed pecking to through-tool coolant. For increments, Nachi General Catalog 2025/2026 p.116 recommends 0.5–1D pecks (0.2–0.5D for small diameters), with retraction to the entrance. Harvey Tool Flat Bottom Drill Guide recommends 0.5–1D subsequent pecks for 38–45 Rc steel. Their ranges overlap at 0.5D; neither is a universal constant-peck specification.
source.policy: Half-diameter is chosen from the overlap of Nachi and Harvey ranges. Extending it to constant increments across materials and depths is step2cam's conservative starting policy, not a universal manufacturer specification. Both intermediate and deep holes use full retract: drills have no through-tool coolant declaration. No universal 5D chip-break/full-retract boundary is asserted. A positive tool peck_mm caps the increment; zero/absent means no cap. At or below 3D a single plunge is used regardless of the cap. Depth is measured from where the drill enters (after roughing, the hole's mouth when the roughing cutter fits the hole or a flats pass at the mouth sweeps the disc over it, otherwise roughing's lowest layer that keeps the bottom allowance above the mouth; without roughing, the stock top as faced; or the top of a recess cut after the hole), including requested breakthrough, excluding the drill point allowance: stock already cut away above the mouth holds no chips. Above 5D, flag the hole as deep and warn that pilot plus deep-hole drilling is not planned; retain the full-retract peck fallback. This warning threshold is the review policy for issue #34, not a universal tool capability limit.
